decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Louise points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Louise keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Louise a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Building regulations
decisions.situation: You stack three blocks. For a moment, the tower stands. Then you discover what your elbow has been planning.

choices.label: Build it again with a wider bottom
Knock down the next tower on purpose
Line the blocks up on the floor

result.title: A better foundation
result.body: The new tower survives your elbow. Your hand brings it down a little later.

journal.text: I rebuilt a block tower with a wider base.

decisions.title: Two is more than one
decisions.situation: Your biscuit breaks in half. There are now two biscuits, although something about the total feels suspicious.

choices.label: Fit the halves back together
Celebrate the extra biscuit
Count all the little crumbs

result.title: The original arrangement
result.body: The edges match. You test them twice before accepting that both pieces were one biscuit.

journal.text: I fitted two broken biscuit halves back together.

decisions.title: Missing person: teddy’s eye
decisions.situation: One of your old teddy’s button eyes comes off. You ask Louise whether teddy needs an ambulance.

choices.label: Help with a supervised repair
Give teddy a pirate patch
Stay with teddy until it is fixed

result.title: Outpatient care
result.body: Louise handles the needle. You choose where the eye belongs.

journal.text: I helped Louise repair my teddy.

decisions.title: A very short biography
decisions.situation: Chloé passes you a homemade book called “People Who Smell Weird”. Your name is on page one. Every other page is blank.

choices.label: Give it a terrible review
Ask why they made it about you
Write their name on every remaining page

result.title: Needs more characters
result.body: You write “repetitive, poorly researched” on the cover. Chloé laughs, then admits they could not think of a second chapter.

journal.text: I reviewed Chloé’s insulting homemade book as a disappointed critic.

decisions.title: Supreme Slide Commander
decisions.situation: Chloé has ranked everyone in the slide queue. They are “Supreme Commander”. You are “Basic Passenger”. They say commanders get two turns.

choices.label: Apply to be Deputy Slide Commander
Take your basic turn
Publish a ranking with them at the bottom

result.title: A top-heavy administration
result.body: Chloé agrees, then everyone else demands a promotion. You end up with nine commanders taking one turn each.

journal.text: I helped dismantle Chloé’s slide hierarchy by getting everyone promoted.

decisions.title: Imaginary friend wanted
decisions.situation: Chloé is alone at break. They say their imaginary friend has moved to a better school. They are interviewing replacements on the empty part of the bench.

choices.label: Help interview the invisible applicants
Apply, despite being inconveniently real
Pretend you have accidentally sat on one

result.title: A crowded bench
result.body: You reject the first applicant for imaginary biting. Chloé rejects the second for actually being a dragon. You run out of break before making an appointment.

journal.text: I helped Chloé interview replacements for an imaginary friend.

decisions.title: Indoor architecture
decisions.situation: Rain cancels your afternoon plans. Two chairs and a blanket suggest a career in questionable structural engineering.

choices.label: Build an elaborate fort
Read by the window
Declare the whole day ruined

result.title: Approved for immediate occupancy
result.body: It collapses twice. The third version has a reading corner.

journal.text: I built a blanket fort that almost met building regulations.

decisions.title: Fun fact about yourself
decisions.situation: You must introduce yourself with one fun fact. The person before you announces they once swallowed a coin. Everyone turns to you expecting escalation.

choices.label: Give your name and disappoint them
Claim you only eat paper money
Recite your entire biography at speed

result.title: No coins were harmed
result.body: You say you like music. A perfectly ordinary fact survives in a room briefly obsessed with swallowing things.

journal.text: I gave a simple introduction after someone set an alarming standard.

decisions.title: The unpaid goblin
decisions.situation: Chloé turns your group presentation into a pitch for an imaginary company. You are listed as “unpaid goblin”. Their dog is CEO. Gabriel asks where the actual research is.

choices.label: Open the real research before the dog gets a salary
Whisper a demand for a better job title
Delete the pitch while they are presenting it

result.title: Goblin saves the meeting
result.body: You present your actual work. Gabriel marks it while Chloé clicks past a slide about office beanbags. The dog receives no academic credit.

journal.text: I rescued our group presentation after Chloé replaced the research with a fake company pitch.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Louise finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Watch it together
Ask to keep the recording private
Defend the bath theory

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Louise remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Louise.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
Follow the trolley out
Perform an increasingly furious dance

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: Doing nothing, attendance required
decisions.situation: You put “Do absolutely nothing” in your calendar. The app sends invitations to a discussion group. Six people accept and one asks about the dress code.

choices.label: Cancel it and protect your hour
Host exactly five minutes of nothing
Send an agenda for competitive relaxing

result.title: A successful cancellation
result.body: You explain that it was private. Someone replies that they were really looking forward to nothing. You enjoy it without them.

journal.text: I cancelled accidental invitations to my free hour.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: The soup tribunal
decisions.situation: You describe a bowl of soup online as “fine”. A stranger accuses you of destroying local culture. They have posted eleven replies and a diagram.

choices.label: Explain that you meant the soup
Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: Any difficult questions?
decisions.situation: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
Let another questioner take this one
Announce that the pigeons work for you

result.title: The method needs work
result.body: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.

journal.text: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Donate €223.72 to the donkey charity
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Return the microphone immediately
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: Serving suggestion: a camera
decisions.situation: An online meal looks so perfect that your ordinary food feels embarrassing. Then the creator posts a behind-the-scenes clip: the garnish is held up with glue.

choices.label: Appreciate that your food is edible
Borrow the arrangement, skip the glue
Decide your food still looks inadequate

result.title: Dinner wins on a technicality
result.body: Your meal lacks dramatic lighting. It also lacks craft adhesive, which feels like a reasonable compromise.

journal.text: I stopped comparing ordinary food with a staged meal photograph.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Marseille needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Weed beside the alarming apron
Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Marseille.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing
Send someone a proper message
Investigate another hour of success

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about
Claim you invented motivational seminars

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Marseille takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: persistent headaches and dizziness. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €20.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

choices.label: Accept hospital assessment
Decline assessment

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
Climb in and ask for paddles
Insist the picture on the box was misleading

result.title: A long public fart
result.body: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.

journal.text: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

decisions.title: Happy statistical decline
decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Celebrate without the comparison chart
Choose one goal that is actually yours
Read every biography before bed

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: The plan met a different day
decisions.situation: While living with Hypertension, you reach an optional household task with less energy than you expected. Yesterday’s plan did not allow for that.

choices.label: Choose a smaller version of the task
Leave the optional task and rest
Push through to satisfy the old plan

result.title: A plan that can bend
result.body: You do one manageable part and leave the rest. An incomplete chore feels less important once it stops being a test.

journal.text: I adjusted an optional task to the energy I had with Hypertension.

result.title: Medical care arranged

decisions.title: Their timeline is not yours
decisions.situation: You read someone else’s account of living with Hypertension. Their progress sounds tidy enough to have been edited, and you begin comparing every part with your own.

choices.label: Step away from the comparison
Write down what is useful to ask about
Keep measuring yourself against the account

result.title: A different person’s account
result.body: You leave the story where it belongs: with the person who wrote it. Your own experience does not need to match its pace.

journal.text: I stepped away from comparing my experience of Hypertension with someone else’s.

decisions.title: A very local tragedy
decisions.situation: On a free history walk in Marseille, the guide points at a laundrette: “A forbidden romance began here.” The owner leans out and asks whether this is about the washing-machine warranty.

choices.label: Stay for both versions
Ask the owner for the real story
Leave before the historical reenactment

result.title: Star-crossed and spin-dried
result.body: The guide describes a doomed affair. The owner describes a parts supplier. You finish the walk unsure which relationship suffered more.

journal.text: I heard two competing tragedies outside a laundrette in Marseille.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
Delete the post without explaining
Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
Change your position and relax your shoulders
Stay exactly as you are

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Marseille unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Marseille.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
Disclose that you eat cabbage
Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Wealth you cannot see
decisions.situation: A free gallery in Marseille displays an empty plinth titled “My Invisible Yacht”. A visitor says only rich people can understand it. You can see the same amount of yacht as everyone else.

choices.label: Ask the guide what the work means
Admire its excellent fuel economy
Pretend to fall overboard

result.title: A surprisingly useful explanation
result.body: The guide says it is about status and imaginary ownership. The visitor looks relieved that somebody has supplied an answer.

journal.text: I asked about an invisible-yacht artwork in Marseille.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

choices.label: Look around for a minute
Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: You are almost in the picture
decisions.situation: An old photograph catches you at the edge of the frame, apparently concentrating on something outside it. You can no longer remember what seemed so important.

choices.label: Enjoy the unfinished little mystery
Write down what you do remember
Build a grand explanation around the pose

result.title: A life outside the frame
result.body: You let the unknown detail remain unknown. The photograph still holds an ordinary moment worth keeping.

decisions.title: The final appeal
decisions.situation: A card-game app informs you that you have been playing an old favourite incorrectly for decades. You dispute this. The rectangle produces a rulebook.

choices.label: Invent a house rule and silence the app
Learn the proper rule and play one game
Read every rule for a loophole

result.title: A local variation
result.body: You mute the little victory tune until it stops judging you. You then award yourself a win under a rule added thirty seconds ago.

journal.text: I invented a house rule after a card-game app challenged the way I played.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Take the next manageable step
Ask whether the intention needs adjusting
Declare yourself hopeless at consistency

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: In loving memory of the wrong man
decisions.situation: A public meeting in Marseille unveils a proposed memorial bench. Its plaque honours a man who is alive, in the room, and asking whether this affects his parking permit.

choices.label: Suggest checking the plaque first
Hear the allegedly deceased man out
Leave before the eulogy

result.title: Death withdrawn from the proposal
result.body: You help redirect the discussion towards correcting the inscription. The man asks to keep “much loved” if possible.

journal.text: I suggested correcting a memorial plaque for a living man in Marseille.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Drink the tap water
Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: A very local tragedy
decisions.situation: On a free history walk in Marseille, the guide points at a laundrette: “A forbidden romance began here.” The owner leans out and asks whether this is about the washing-machine warranty.

choices.label: Stay for both versions
Ask the owner for the real story
Leave before the historical reenactment

result.title: Star-crossed and spin-dried
result.body: The guide describes a doomed affair. The owner describes a parts supplier. You finish the walk unsure which relationship suffered more.

journal.text: I heard two competing tragedies outside a laundrette in Marseille.

decisions.title: It cannot have been this bad
decisions.situation: You revisit a comedy you have called your favourite for years. Ten minutes in, a man falls into a bucket for the fourth time. You appear to have remembered a much better programme.

choices.label: Admit your taste has improved
Work out what you used to enjoy
Watch the whole thing out of loyalty

result.title: The bucket loses a fan
result.body: You stop watching without trying to defend your younger self in court. There are other ways to spend the evening.

journal.text: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.

decisions.title: Apparently you ate
decisions.situation: A younger person points at your outfit and says, “You ate.” You have no food on you. They add, “No crumbs.” This is getting less clear.

choices.label: Ask whether this is a compliment
Reply, “Thank you. It was delicious.”
Announce that you can feed yourself

result.title: Breakfast has nothing to do with it
result.body: It is a compliment. You thank them and ask for a translation before anyone says anything else about your digestion.
